done_when: A client repo upgrades Forge through one fix whose pull request passes Forge's check

findings.body: The handoff runs only inside the newly installed checker. A client base pinned to v1.1.0 runs its existing workflow, which installs v1.1.0 (`v1.1.0:src/forge/sync.py:264-266`); that release's `pr_check` has no handoff (`v1.1.0:src/forge/prcheck.py:35-76`). Thus an upgrade PR is judged by the old release, not the release it pins, and the new release-tag validation is never reached. The compatible `tree` field may let the old check pass, including for a changed pin without `v`, but it does not deliver the required pinned-release check. Put the release selection in a path the base workflow actually executes.
findings.title: Not done: An upgrade pull request passes Forge's check

findings.body: The upgrade case calls `_older_build`, which copies this checkout's Forge and changes only its version string. Its apparent v1.0.9 checker therefore contains the new handoff that a released older checker lacks; the `uv` stub then runs this checkout again. This test can pass while a real client workflow never installs or invokes the PR's pinned release. Exercise an actual released base checker and the generated workflow's install path, faking only the external installer.
findings.title: Not done: tests/test_upgrade_check.py

findings.body: The reported six-case walkthrough claims an upgrade from a v1.0.9 base handed off to the pinned release. The supplied upgrade path uses the relabeled current-source build and an installer stub that launches the current-source Forge. It never walks an upgrade through a released base's workflow, so it skips the covered pinned-release install. Repeat that walkthrough with the released base and verify which Forge version actually runs.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

why: Upgrading Forge in a client repo is blocked: the upgrade pull request can never pass Forge's check, close calls it clean with stale synced files, and the default branch refuses every command until the upgrade merges
